place: A small town (about 4,400 people) in the interior of Minas Gerais, Brazil (Aguanil, Cerrado / Atlantic Forest transition); state figures where no municipal figure exists
about: Every place-specific figure the town generator uses for a small town in interior Minas Gerais, Brazil, with its source. The reference municipality is Aguanil, MG (IBGE code 3100807; 4,357 residents in the 2022 Census; Campo das Vertentes / south-central Minas): its Census 2022 age structure, households, tenure and religion, and its 2024 municipal accounts, are used directly; state (Minas Gerais) figures are used where no municipal figure exists, and national ones where no state figure exists. Fortnightly wages and payments are the monthly Brazilian figures converted (x 12 / 26) because the structure pays on 14 days. Values still marked placeholder say what they were estimated from. A world for another place and time is another profile; the platform's code holds none of these (docs/profiles.md). SINCE 2026-10-09 (employment.*): the profile states the share of employees' jobs that are registered and the share and kinds of own-account work; the town holds the own-account traders (about 5% of people in work), and the other kinds are still drawn as employees.

sources.frictions: Everyday frictions (docs/behaviour/frictions.md): what goes wrong, how often, and how the bodies that hear it work. Read by the generator only for a town whose spec has `living`.
sources.frictions.per_adult_bps_per_year: Of adults, the share who had each kind of problem, a year: half the share who had it in the last two years in World Justice Project, Global Insights on Access to Justice 2019 (General Population Poll 2017-18, about 1,000 respondents a country; the summary statistics workbook was opened; national, and for Brazil and Mexico the three largest cities only). landlord: a problem with a landlord over agreements, payments, repairs, deposits or eviction (4.5% in two years; all of it is given to disrepair here, which overstates repairs: the town has no other landlord problem of the kind yet). wages: difficulty obtaining wages or employment benefits agreed in advance (4.2%). bill: major disruption of a utility's supply or incorrect billing (17.9%; all of it is given to wrong bills). benefits: difficulty obtaining public benefits or government assistance (2.4%). goods: a consumer problem (32.0%) less the utility share, since the survey's consumer problems include it (derived; poor professional services are in it too). The generator turns each into a rate for those exposed (a let dwelling, a job, a customer, a claim) with the town's own counts. Halving a two-year share understates a yearly one where people have a problem in both years (to confirm against a yearly survey).
sources.frictions.put_right_on_asking_bps: Asked to put it right, how often the other side does. PLACEHOLDERS, every one: each stands at the share of people with any problem who say it is done and fully resolved (54.7%: World Justice Project, Global Insights on Access to Justice 2019 (General Population Poll 2017-18, about 1,000 respondents a country; the summary statistics workbook was opened; national, and for Brazil and Mexico the three largest cities only)), which is an outcome of everything people tried, not the rate at which the other side agrees when asked: to replace with a figure by kind of problem.
sources.frictions.pay_short_by_bps: PLACEHOLDER: by how much pay that comes short is short (5%). No figure was found for this place.
sources.frictions.bill_over_bps: PLACEHOLDER: by how much a wrong bill overstates what was used (30%). No figure was found.
sources.frictions.goods_faulty_share_bps: PLACEHOLDER: of a shopping trip's goods, the share that is faulty when some are (a quarter). No figure was found.
sources.frictions.repair_hours: PLACEHOLDER: the hours of a builder's hand a repair takes (two days' work). No figure was found for a typical rental repair.
sources.frictions.support: processing_days: PLACEHOLDER (a fortnight); no figure was opened for this place. wrong_refusal_bps: of claims that qualify, the share wrongly refused. FITTED in the 1,000-person town of the first profile (7% of qualifying claims gives about as many refusals a year as 6% of adults, its survey share with difficulty obtaining public benefits, counting the refusals that are right), and for every other place scaled by its own survey share against that one: a stand-in until a place's own rate of decisions changed on review is found.
sources.frictions.venues: tribunal_days: PLACEHOLDER (six weeks); no median time to disposal was found for this place. answer_days (the time the other side is given to answer a desk), tribunal_fee_hours_of_pay (the fee as hours of a shop worker's pay), cases_per_day (cases a desk's staff decide in a day) and uphold_without_proof_bps (how often a desk finds for someone with nothing to show, where the other side cannot say from its records): PLACEHOLDERS; no figure was opened.
sources.outlook: How people start out in what they trust (docs/behaviour/citizen.md, 'The record'). National figures for Brazil, not the region's: none by region was found. trust: the share with 'a great deal' or 'quite a lot' of confidence in each kind of institution (`government`, `policing`: the police, `courts`, the civil service, banks, the press, labour unions, churches or religious organisations, major companies); people_bps: the share who say most people can be trusted. World Values Survey and European Values Study, joint wave 7 (fieldwork 2017 to 2022), as Our World in Data publishes it (ourworldindata.org/grapher/trust-state-institutions-wvs, trust-organizations-wvs, self-reported-trust-attitudes), opened 2026-10-11 through a tool that returns a page's figures in summary: to confirm against the survey's own tables. The share is read as the mean level of trust a person starts with, which is a simplification (a share above a threshold is not a mean). Not stated, so the citizen's own placeholders apply (to source: the survey's question on freedom of choice and control over one's life, its mean and spread, needs the microdata): how much control over their lives people feel (outlook.agency).
sources.outlook.residence: PLACEHOLDER: no figure for how long people have lived at their address was found for Brazil on a page opened. Borrowed from Australia's (the only place whose figures were opened), for lack of any: ABS, 2021 Census, 'Population movement in Australia' (released 8 November 2022; abs.gov.au/articles/population-movement-australia), opened 2026-10-11: 53.1% of the population lived at the same address five years before the Census; 14.3% changed address within Australia in the year before; 0.7% had lived overseas a year before. Bands here: under 1 year = 14.3 + 0.7 = 15.0%; 1 to under 5 = the rest (31.9%); 5 and over = 53.1%. They are built from the one-year and five-year mobility rates, so the 1 to under 5 band is the remainder, and the 5-and-over share is the share at the same address five years earlier (population aged 5 and over, not adults only). National figures, not Victoria's: the Victoria figures were not found on an opened page. The open band is read as 5 to 15 years by the generator. Brazil's own are probably different (to source: Census or housing-survey tables of years since moving in).
sources.outlook.job_tenure: How long employed people have been with their current employer (starting attachment to the trade). OECD, 'Employment by job tenure intervals' (dataset OECD.ELS.SAE DSD_TENURE@DF_TENURE_FREQ, measure TENURE_EMP, share of employment by time with the current employer; both sexes, all ages), national figures for Brazil, 2024; read from the OECD SDMX API (sdmx.oecd.org/public/rest/data/OECD.ELS.SAE,DSD_TENURE@DF_TENURE_FREQ) on 2026-10-11, the response opened and the figures copied: under 1 year, 1 to under 3, 3 to under 5, 5 to under 10, 10 and over. National, not the region's: none by region was found. It covers the employed (employees and the self-employed), where a person's tenure is the time in the present job. The open band (10 and over) is read as 10 to 30 years by the generator. The shares sum to 99.9 to 100 in the source and are scaled to 10000.
sources.employment.registered_bps: IBGE, PNAD Continua quarterly, SIDRA table 4097 (people employed by position in occupation), Minas Gerais, 2nd quarter 2026 (https://apisidra.ibge.gov.br/values/t/4097/n3/31/v/4090/p/202602/c11913/all; opened and read by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-09): of 5,616 thousand private-sector employees (domestic workers apart), 1,445 thousand have no signed work card (sem carteira), 25.7%; so 74.3% are registered. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Jobs an employer does not register"): each employer of a kind registers this share of its own jobs; a job outside it is paid whole, nothing is withheld and no report names the worker. The same share is given for shops, factories and construction because the source divides employees by status, not by kind of employer (its rates by activity count own-account workers too, and are not used). Nothing inspects: the share is a stated fact of the place.
sources.employment.own_account: [MIXED] Share: the same SIDRA table: 2,740 thousand own-account workers (conta propria) of 11,013 thousand employed in Minas Gerais, 24.9% (farming included: the state figure). Kinds: ILOSTAT (the ILO's SDMX service, sdmx.ilo.org/rest/data/ILO,<dataflow>/<country>.A....?format=csv&startPeriod=2018; each file opened and the figures read from it by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-09), dataflow DF_EMP_TEMP_SEX_STE_ECO_NB, Brazil, 2025 (source: PNAD Continua), own-account workers outside agriculture by ISIC section: trade (G) 21.1%, construction (F) 15.8%, other services (S) 12.8%, transport (H) 12.3%, manufacturing (C) 9.2%, accommodation and food (I) 7.5%, professional activities (M) 7.5%, the other sections 13.8%. National, not Minas Gerais. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/entry.md, "A person working for themself"): the share is of people in work at the start; the town holds the kinds that trade (each person in a business of one, from a pitch in the town's market or from home) and draws people of the other kinds in jobs, as before. PLACEHOLDER within it: the even split of trade between a pitch and home (no survey of where traders work from was opened), and seven days of stock. So of the place's 24.9%, the town holds the traders: about 5% of people in work.
sources.currency: Brazilian real, in centavos: written R$ before the amount, or in words as reais and centavos. ISO 4217: BRL, two decimal places. How its people write money: a comma before the decimals, points between thousands, R$ before the digits with a space ("R$ 1.234,56"). Unicode CLDR (cldr-json, cldr-numbers-full/main/pt/numbers.json, opened 2026-10-08): decimal ',', group '.', currency pattern '¤ #,##0.00' (the data is Portuguese for Brazil by CLDR's default; the page does not say so itself). The Manual de Redação da Presidência da República and ANBIMA's manual were not opened (a web search found them; no text was read). "Conto" is removed from the unit words: in every dictionary opened (Priberam, https://dicionario.priberam.org/conto: "mil escudos"; Dictionary.com: "1000 escudos", "1000 milreis", "an unofficial Brazilian monetary unit worth 1000 cruzeiros") it is a thousand of the unit, never one real, and none of them says it is used for one real, so "5 conto" must not be read as five reais (it is refused).

sources.rents_per_month: Derived, not observed: IBGE, Pesquisa de Orcamentos Familiares 2017-18, SIDRA table 6715, Minas Gerais: average monetary rent paid R$92.49 a family a month across all families (opened 2026-10-08); divided by the renting share of occupied dwellings in Minas Gerais, 22.5% (Census 2022, table 9929: 1,693,310 of 7,534,797) = R$411.6 per renting family in 2017-18; times the IPCA from January 2018 to August 2026, 1.548 (Banco Central SGS 433, opened) = R$637 a month (two-bedroom). Other sizes are 0.75x (one bedroom), 1.25x (three bedrooms, house) and 1.6x (four bedrooms): an assumption, not data. Census 2022 did not publish rent amounts; the state mean is used for a small town (likely high).

sources.retirement_age: Placeholder / closest fit: 65. Under Emenda Constitucional 103/2019 the permanent old-age retirement age is 65 for men and 62 for women (urban workers, INSS); rural workers 60 and 55 (Lei 8.213/1991, art. 48 par. 1); the low-income old-age benefit (BPC/LOAS, Lei 8.742/1993) starts at 65. The profile holds one age; see the report on structural gaps. Since 2026-10-08 people here stop work at ages of their own, drawn from labour_force_share_by_age; this age is still the one the profile's other figures turn on (the retired's savings, the end of the payments for those out of work, a retirement fund's access) and the top of the working ages the measures use. The pension's age is the payment's own (support.payments).
sources.retiree_savings: Placeholder: the reference profile's range scaled by 0.2 (see savings_by_age).
sources.support.payments: [The pension:] Minimum wage R$1,621 a month from 1 January 2026: Decreto no 12.797, 23 December 2025, art. 1 (opened at planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2023-2026/2025/decreto/d12797.htm, 2026-10-08), the floor of INSS old-age benefits and of the BPC (Lei 8.742/1993) at 65. Paid every 30 days (a monthly payment; the reference profile pays every 14). The 13th payment is not modelled. [The payment to those out of work:] Closest fit, not a match: Bolsa Familia average benefit R$671.54 a family in August 2026 (Ministerio do Desenvolvimento e Assistencia Social, news item "Bolsa Familia chega a mais de 19,19 milhoes de familias em agosto", gov.br/mds, read in a search summary; the page itself returned an error when fetched). A household-income-tested payment to poor families, paid monthly; from age 18. Seguro-desemprego cannot be expressed. See the report on structural gaps. SHAPE (2026-10-08, track D of docs/design/profile-depth.md): support is now a list of payments, each a rule in three parts: who qualifies, how much, for how long (docs/behaviour/boundary.md); the law is published and the payments office reads it. The payments for those out of work end the year before the profile's retirement age (to_age): the rule the generator applied to every profile until now, written into the payment, where it can be changed. The pension is paid from the INSS (this note: the floor of INSS old-age benefits). STAND-IN KEPT: the payment to those out of work is still the Bolsa Família average benefit paid flat to anyone out of work, because this note gives the average and not the programme's rule. The rule can now be said: a household's payment (`amount.household`, `per_member`, `per_child`), for households whose declared income a head is under a line (`who.income_under`, per head), claimed by the household's head, whether or not anyone is out of work. The figures (the income line, the sum a family, the sum for each young child) are for the author to add with their source. Seguro-desemprego can now be said too (a share of previous pay, for so many days, on a record of contributions); no figures are in this note.

sources.labour_force_participation_bps: Derived estimate: IBGE, PNAD Continua 2nd quarter 2026, Minas Gerais (SIDRA table 4093): participation 64.0% of people aged 14 and over (11.45 million in the labour force of 17.89 million); rescaled to ages 15-64 using the Census 2022 age structure of the state (14.3 million aged 15-64) and an assumed 0.65 million workers aged 65 and over, giving about 74%. The 65+ assumption is not data.
sources.labour_force_share_by_age: ILOSTAT, 'Labour force participation rate by sex and age (%)', five-year bands (dataflow DF_EAP_DWAP_SEX_AGE_RT, https://sdmx.ilo.org/rest/data/ILO,DF_EAP_DWAP_SEX_AGE_RT/all?startPeriod=2019; the data file opened and these figures read from it, 2026-10-08), persons, Brazil, national, annual 2025, from IBGE's PNAD Contínua: ages 25 to 54, 80.376%; 55 to 59, 63.138%; 60 to 64, 46.679%; 65 and over, 16.059%. National, not Minas Gerais (no table by age for the region was found); not checked against IBGE (SIDRA)'s own table (to confirm). How it is used: the first band is the reference; someone in the labour force stops work at the start of a later band with the chance these shares give, and those still in at the last band never stop. The survey's last band is open (65 and over), so nobody is drawn to stop after 65, and those who work on are older on average than they are in fact: to split when the shares at 65 to 69, 70 to 74 and 75 and over are opened. The profile's own participation figure (labour_force_participation_bps) still says how many are in the labour force at the reference ages; this curve says only how that share falls with age.

sources.public_finance.income_tax: Lei 15.270/2025, art. 3-A of the personal income tax law (opened at planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2023-2026/2025/lei/l15270.htm, 2026-10-08): reduction of the tax so that income up to R$5,000 a month (R$60,000 a year) pays none, and a declining reduction R$978.62 - 0.133145 x income from R$5,000.01 to R$7,350; no reduction above R$7,350. The profile expresses it as three annual steps: 0% to R$60,000, a 40.81% marginal band to R$88,200 (27.5% plus the phase-out), then 27.5%: an approximation (it ignores the monthly simplified deduction of R$607.20). Federal tax; not the municipality's. [Was the note on levy_bps:] INSS employee contribution, 2026: 7.5% to R$1,621, 9% to R$2,902.84, 12% to R$4,354.27, 14% to R$8,475.55 (Portaria Interministerial MPS/MF no 13, 9 January 2026; table read in the gov.br/inss page via search summary). At a R$3,000 wage the contribution is 8.3% (computed here), used as the flat levy. It funds the INSS, not general revenue, and its ceiling cannot be expressed. [Was the note on levy_from:] Placeholder: the INSS contribution applies from the first real earned. SHAPE (2026-10-08, track E of docs/design/profile-depth.md): the law is now a list of charges, each with what it is charged on, its schedule, its reliefs and whom it is paid to (docs/behaviour/public-finance.md). The income tax keeps the author's three steps (an approximation of the reduction, as said above). UN-FOLDED: the flat levy of 8.3% that stood for the INSS contribution is now the contribution's own table as this note gives it, by slices of a year's pay (twelve times the monthly limits: 7.5% to R$19,452.00, 9% to R$34,834.08, 12% to R$52,251.24, 14% to the ceiling of R$101,706.60, nothing above), paid to the INSS and not to general revenue. The thirteenth salary is not reckoned.

sources.public_finance.grants_per_resident_per_y: Tesouro Nacional, SICONFI open API (apidatalake.tesouro.gov.br), DCA-Anexo I-C, Prefeitura Municipal de Aguanil, 2024 (4,362 residents): general-purpose transfers of R$25.51 million = FPM R$18.56 million + ITR R$25,372 + mineral/oil compensations R$1.34 million + the state's share of ICMS, IPVA, IPI and CIDE R$5.58 million, i.e. R$5,849 a resident. Transfers tied to health (SUS) and education (FUNDEB, FNDE), which the generator funds separately for the clinic and school, are left out. Opened 2026-10-08. Total revenue was R$46.1 million (R$10,577 a resident), of which own taxes were R$1.13 million. FLAGGED FOR THIS PROFILE'S AUTHOR (2026-10-09, the second live check, finding 14): this is the municipality's whole general transfer for each resident, which there pays for everything it runs (welfare, schools, health, administration, debt). The town generated from this profile runs only waste collection, the upkeep of its parks, hall and roads, a park and some roads a year and a wildlife survey, so its opening budget spends a small part of what this grant pays in and the rest piles up in its account. Not changed here: the figure is right for what it says it is. What is wanted is the grant for the functions the town has: the same source's spending by purpose would give the share (not opened).

sources.nature.species: Callithrix penicillata (native to the Cerrado and Atlantic Forest edge). In Cerrado habitats (cerradao and dense cerrado) of the Brazilian Central Plateau: groups of 4 to 11, home range 8.25 to 18.5 ha, density 0.4 to 0.82 individuals a hectare, higher in gallery forest (Miranda and Faria 2001, Brazilian Journal of Biology / Brazilian Journal of Biology 61; found via search, paper not opened; to confirm). Density 0.8 in woodland and riverbank and 0.4 in scrub; growth, mortality and dispersal are placeholders. | Myrmecophaga tridactyla, Vulnerable (IUCN Red List; ICMBio Livro Vermelho 2018; to confirm). Density about 0.2 to 0.4 animals per square kilometre in Cerrado (0.002 to 0.004 per hectare) and a home range of the order of 300 ha (Medri and Mourao 2005 and Cerrado studies; from memory; to confirm). Growth, mortality and dispersal are placeholders (one pup a year; road-kill is a leading cause of death). | Turdus rufiventris (sabia-laranjeira), the national bird of Brazil, common and conspicuous in towns and woodland. Density and home range are placeholders (no source retrieved; a typical passerine territory is about 1 ha). | Caiman latirostris, found in wetlands and rivers of the Atlantic Forest and Cerrado; in Rio Doce State Park, Minas Gerais, an encounter rate of 4.01 individuals a kilometre of water body was recorded (found via search from Brazilian herpetological literature, paper not opened; to confirm). Converted by the cell size to about 1.6 an hectare of riverbank cell (an estimate); the wetland density, home range, growth and mortality are placeholders. IUCN Least Concern (to confirm). Tolerance of pollution is a placeholder.
